content_units: Reception Dancefloor Plan

A balanced 20-song wedding reception playlist for ages 18 to 70, built to stay family-friendly, highly danceable, and varied across decades. It is split into a smooth warm-up, a high-energy peak run, and a big sing-along finish, with no artist used more than twice.
20-Song Cross-Generational Playlist
Section   Artist   Song   Decade   Why it works
1   Warm-up   Earth, Wind & Fire   September   1970s   Instant feel-good groove across generations
2   Warm-up   ABBA   Dancing Queen   1970s   Familiar, joyful, and easy to fill the floor early
3   Warm-up   Whitney Houston   I Wanna Dance with Somebody   1980s   Big chorus and clean, upbeat energy
4   Warm-up   Michael Jackson   Billie Jean   1980s   Strong groove without going too hard too soon
5   Warm-up   Madonna   Holiday   1980s   Light, fun, and easy for mixed-age guests
6   Warm-up   Spice Girls   Wannabe   1990s   Nostalgic and playful, especially for group dancing
7   Peak dance floor   Mark Ronson feat. Bruno Mars   Uptown Funk   2010s   Modern classic with broad age appeal
8   Peak dance floor   OutKast   Hey Ya!   2000s   Fast lift in energy and universally recognizable
9   Peak dance floor   Black Eyed Peas   I Gotta Feeling   2000s   Wedding-friendly party anthem
10   Peak dance floor   Dua Lipa   Don't Start Now   2010s   Contemporary disco-pop that works for all ages
11   Peak dance floor   Usher feat. Lil Jon & Ludacris   Yeah!   2000s   Strong floor-packer for younger and middle-age guests
12   Peak dance floor   Lady Gaga   Just Dance   2000s   Keeps momentum up with a clean pop hook
13   Peak dance floor   Earth, Wind & Fire   Let's Groove   1980s   Funk energy that reconnects older and younger guests
14   Peak dance floor   The Killers   Mr. Brightside   2000s   Big crossover hit with shout-along appeal
15   Sing-along finale   Journey   Don't Stop Believin'   1980s   One of the strongest all-room sing-alongs
16   Sing-along finale   Neil Diamond   Sweet Caroline   1960s   Crowd participation comes naturally
17   Sing-along finale   Bon Jovi   Livin' on a Prayer   1980s   High-energy chorus for late-night unity
18   Sing-along finale   Queen   Don't Stop Me Now   1970s   Uplifting closer-build with wide recognition
19   Sing-along finale   Taylor Swift   Shake It Off   2010s   Keeps younger guests engaged while staying family-friendly
20   Sing-along finale   The Beatles   Twist and Shout   1960s   Classic, joyful, and ideal for a final shared burst
Flow Notes for the DJ Set
-   Warm-up:   Tracks 1-6 build familiarity without exhausting the room too early.
-   Peak dance floor:   Tracks 7-14 lean into nonstop movement, with funk, pop, hip-hop, and indie crossover.
-   Sing-along finale:   Tracks 15-20 are built for arms-up, full-room choruses, and a celebratory ending.
Quick Actions
Copy Playlist
Build in Apple Music
Source-Friendly Set Notes
- Clean/radio edits are recommended for tracks like “Yeah!” and “Hey Ya!” for a fully family-friendly reception.
- This sequence spans the 1960s through the 2010s to keep the age range well covered.
- Artist repeat check: only Earth, Wind & Fire appears twice; all others appear once.
